atoms.text: The SMART method helps us set realistic goals that make sense.

trainers.instruction: Match the descriptions to the terms.

atoms.b: Something that clearly defines what you want to achieve.
atoms.sound: Specific. Something that clearly defines what you want to achieve.

atoms.b: Something that can be measured with milestones.
atoms.sound: Measurable. Something that can be measured with milestones.

atoms.b: Something that is realistic based on your time, skills and support.
atoms.sound: Achievable. Something that is realistic based on your time, skills and support.

atoms.b: Something that matters to you and keeps you motivated.
atoms.sound: Relevant. Something that matters to you and keeps you motivated.

atoms.b: Something that has a deadline to help you focus.
atoms.sound: Time-limited. Something that has a deadline to help you focus.

b.text: Chris wants to improve his passing accuracy in football.

flip.text: Chris wants to improve his passing accuracy in football.

b.text: Chris wants to get better at football.

feedback.end: It is more specific to choose a certain skill you want to improve in. This can make the goal of getting better at football more realistic.

b.text: Laura wants to get 8/10 or more in the spelling test.

flip.text: Laura wants to get 8/10 or more in the spelling test.

b.text: Laura wants to get good marks in the next spelling test.

feedback.end: It is easier to track your progress towards achieving a certain mark than to simply say you want to do well. This can help you stay focused.

atoms.hint: Measurable means that you define milestones and can track progress. There is a clear end point.

b.text: Delilah wants to do 4 hours of exercise a week.

flip.text: Delilah wants to do 4 hours of exercise a week.

b.text: Delilah wants to do 10 hours of exercise a week.

feedback.end: Limiting your goal can make it more realistic that you achieve it. Taking on too much can make working towards your goal feel overwhelming.

b.text: James wants to pass his grade 2 violin exam.

flip.text: James wants to pass his grade 2 violin exam.

b.text: James’ dad wants him to pass his grade 2 violin exam.

atoms.hint: Relevant means that a goal is important to the person who has to take the steps to reach it, not anyone else.

feedback.end: Working towards a goal requires a lot of motivation, which is why you should focus on setting goals that are important to you.

b.text: Nick wants to learn a magic trick in the next week.

flip.text: Nick wants to learn a magic trick in the next week.

b.text: Nick wants to learn a magic trick.

feedback.end: Making a deadline or setting a time frame in which you want to reach your goal can help you stay focused.
